hockey_player.evidence: Helmets, skates, and gloves are clearly visible at full size, but the stick shaft is too thin and the blade is too small, causing the hockey read to vanish at small scales.

toy.evidence: Massive heads, stubby limbs, bright flat colors, and thick outlines strongly convey a plastic toy or bobblehead aesthetic at all scales.

answer.best_row: Bottom row, because the forward-leaning skating poses and sliding pose clearly communicate hockey momentum, unlike the stiff vertical poses in the top row.
changes: stick thickness 0.02 of height -> 0.08 of height
blade length 0.10 of height -> 0.25 of height
shoulder width 0.30 of height -> 0.40 of height
worst: Stick shafts are too thin and completely disappear at the downscaled size.
Stick blades are too short and lack the distinct L-shape of a hockey stick.
Top-left orange player holds the stick perfectly vertical like a staff, breaking the hockey silhouette.
works: High contrast between the warm orange and deep blue jerseys makes team identification instant.
Oversized helmets with thick padding perfectly sell the toy look.
Thick black outlines help the figures pop against the white ice.
